lede: Mountlake Terrace keeps Christmas close to home: one big evening at City Hall where school choirs sing, Santa shows up with the fire department and the city lights its tree.
celebrates: The city's signature holiday event is the Holiday Tree Lighting at City Hall on 58th Avenue West, run by Mountlake Terrace Recreation and Parks for more than four decades. Choirs from local elementary schools sing carols, the high school band plays holiday songs, and Santa arrives along with South County Fire. The city hands out free cookies and cocoa before a 20 foot Christmas tree lights up in Jerry Smith Plaza. The city also lights a tree on top of the water tower at Jack Long Park. Mountlake Terrace High School hosts its own Breakfast in Santa's Workshop with music groups, pancakes and Santa photos.
lastyear: On Friday, December 5, 2025, Mountlake Terrace held its 42nd Annual Holiday Tree Lighting at 6 pm at the Jerry Smith Town Center Plaza next to City Hall. The city billed it as a free community event with local school choirs, free cookies and cocoa, and a visit from Santa and South County Fire. The traditional tree on top of the water tower at Jack Long Park was lit at the same moment. With nearby streets closed, the city suggested guests ride light rail to Mountlake Terrace Station.
facts: Mountlake Terrace was built on the site of a World War II landing field. The developers named it for the views: from parts of the land you could see Mount Rainier and Lake Washington, and the old runway looked a bit like a terrace. Cinder block houses went up assembly line style, and by 1954 more than 5,000 people lived there. Residents voted 517 to 483 to become a city on November 23, 1954, and the new city had to borrow $5 just to file its incorporation papers.
trains: Mountlake Terrace has its own Link light rail stop. Mountlake Terrace Station opened in August 2024 as part of the 8.5 mile Lynnwood Link extension of the 1 Line. The elevated station straddles 236th Street SW at the transit center, a short walk from City Hall and the library, so families can ride straight to the tree lighting. Sounder N Line trains and Amtrak Cascades stop in nearby Edmonds. The Northwest Railway Museum in Snoqualmie has run Santa Trains every December since 1969.

kidfact: Mountlake Terrace got its name from what people could see there: a mountain, Mount Rainier, and a lake, Lake Washington. The flat old airplane runway looked like a terrace.
faq: Where is the Mountlake Terrace tree lighting?

The Holiday Tree Lighting takes place at City Hall, 23204 58th Ave W, in Jerry Smith Plaza, where the city lights a 20 foot Christmas tree. The event usually falls on the first Friday evening in December, and the city posts details on its Tree Lighting page and social media.
Is the Mountlake Terrace tree lighting free?

Yes. The city describes the tree lighting as a free community event, and it hands out free cookies and cocoa. Families can listen to local school choirs and the high school band, then see Santa and South County Fire before the tree is lit. No tickets or registration are needed.
How do I get to the Mountlake Terrace tree lighting by train?

Ride Link light rail to Mountlake Terrace Station on the 1 Line. Sound Transit says the station is a short walk from City Hall and the library. In 2025 the city closed nearby streets for the event and pointed guests to the light rail station, which makes the train an easy way in.
What other tree does Mountlake Terrace light?

Along with the 20 foot tree at City Hall, the city lights a traditional tree on top of the water tower at Jack Long Park. In 2025 both trees were switched on at the same time during the Holiday Tree Lighting, so families can spot the water tower tree glowing over the neighborhood afterward.
